TARGET FILE (already exists, ~344 lines): `/opt/nxeon-wt-kbchat/lib/kb-system.ts` — it currently exports `const KB_SYSTEM` (a big knowledge-base string). Your job: RESEARCH the whole app deeply, then REWRITE that file to be far more comprehensive AND add a structured page map.

STEP 1 — RESEARCH broadly (read a lot):
- Read the current `lib/kb-system.ts` and `lib/kb-faq.ts` first (don't lose facts already captured — prices, promo, plans).
- Enumerate EVERY real page/route: `find app -name "page.tsx"` and read the important marketing pages (home, /pricing, /hosting, /vps, game servers, /domains, email, website builder, migrations, /trust or security, free tools, /blog, /contact, legal). Note the exact URL path of each.
- Understand the CUSTOMER PORTAL flows: deploy wizard, server tabs/management, migrations wizard, billing/invoices, SSL, backups, SFTP/file manager, teams, domains, email mailboxes. (grep components/ and app/ for these.)
- Understand HOW THINGS WORK end-to-end: signup → order → provision (pending→live→SSL→app install) → manage; the free-migration flow; billing (monthly/annual terms, first-charge timing, auto-charge/dunning, coupons); one-click apps (WordPress etc.); PHP switcher.
- Note the SUPPORT model: live chat + human handoff, business-day follow-ups.
- Read `DOCUMENTATION.md` and/or `app/admin/docs` if present for authoritative internal flow docs.
Do NOT invent prices/specs/SLAs — ground everything in the repo. Keep all real prices already in the file (shared: Starter $2.99 / Business $4.99 / Pro $8.99; VPS Nano $6.49 / Starter $8.99 / Standard $12.99 / Pro $20.99 / Max $32.99; game/email/nxcloud tiers; term discounts Annual 20% / Biennial 30% / Triennial 40%; first-month-free is SHARED-HOSTING-ONLY).

STEP 2 — REWRITE `/opt/nxeon-wt-kbchat/lib/kb-system.ts` with TWO exports:

(a) `export const KB_SYSTEM = ` + a template string — a DEEP operator knowledge base. Expand well beyond the current version: for every product include plans/prices/specs/who-it's-for/the sales angle; document every major flow step-by-step (signup, order, provisioning states, migration, billing, SSL, backups, email, one-click apps, domain registration); cover policies (support hours/channels, business-day follow-up, refunds only if real, security/uptime posture); and a clear "WHERE TO SEND PEOPLE" section listing the real page paths and when to link each. Keep the "DO NOT CLAIM / hand off to a human" guardrail section. Be genuinely comprehensive — 500-800+ lines is welcome. Real content only, no placeholders.

(b) `export const KB_PAGES: { path: string; title: string; desc: string }[] = [ ... ]` — a canonical map of the real linkable pages (exact paths like "/pricing", "/hosting", "/vps", "/domains", "/blog", "/contact", etc.), each with a short human title and a one-line description of what's there and when to send someone. Only include pages you CONFIRMED exist as routes. This lets the assistant link accurately and lets the UI show page suggestions.

Keep it to this one file, both exports. Do not touch any other file. When done, report: final line count, how many pages are in KB_PAGES, and any new facts/flows you documented that weren't in the previous version.

6711 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md
=====
# Nxeon — the internal manual

The single reference for how this platform actually works: what each feature does, which file does
it, how it fails, and how you diagnose it at 3am. Rendered privately at **`/admin/docs`**, which
splits this file into searchable sections at every `##` heading.

**Read this first.** Three rules govern the whole document:

1. **Reference leads, history follows.** Parts I–VII are reference. The dated change log is Part
   VIII, at the bottom, kept verbatim.
2. **Every `file:line` here was opened and read.** Line numbers drift as several agents edit this
   tree concurrently — treat them as "this function, roughly here", and grep the quoted symbol if a
   number has slipped.
3. **This manual does not overclaim.** The single recurring defect in this codebase is *a surface
   reporting an outcome it never verified*. A manual that asserted features work because the code
   looks complete would be that same bug in a new place. Where something is simulated, partial, or
   saved-and-never-read, the chapter says so, and **Known gaps — the honest inventory** collects
   every instance.

Companion documents — read them, do not edit them:

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` | Line-by-line verification of a 24-hour engineering session against the live tree. Its "top 10 gaps" is the best map of trust debt in this repo. |
| `docs/QA-PRELAUNCH.md` | Pre-launch QA sweep. Source of the cross-tenant email-takeover finding. |
| `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md` | The **customer-journey rehearsal** (2026-07-26): the whole funnel driven in a real browser on staging, every finding tagged `[RAN]` or `[READ]`. Source of the three launch blockers, the 2FA lockout, the capitalised-email lockout and the NAT-flush finding. Most of it is now fixed — commits `7490131` and `3aa24d7`. Its *"Verified correct — do not re-open"* section is the shortest honest list of what works. |
| `docs/MIGRATION-REHEARSAL.md` | The first end-to-end migration rehearsal against a purpose-built messy source server. Nine engine defects, none of which a test or a type would have caught. Fixed in `fd71056`. |
| `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` | 28 numbered real-world migration failures with the fix for each. Acceptance criteria for the migration engine. |
| `docs/MIGRATION.md` | Moving the Nxeon *platform itself* to another box — not customer migration. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Agent-facing conventions and safety rules. |
| `ROADMAP.md` | Known to be wrong in both directions. See Known gaps before trusting it. |

### Live states an operator has to act on

None is a bug in the code and none is visible from the admin console. All are true right now, verified
2026-07-27 at commit `1c3c00c`.

**1. Platform transactional email is now DKIM-signed — one confirmation step remains before the
verification gate can be armed.** `dkim._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` **now publishes a valid DKIM1 RSA key**
(verified 2026-07-27 resolving against 1.1.1.1 **and** 8.8.8.8), and the stale
`nxeon._domainkey.nxeon.cloud` has been **deleted** (now NXDOMAIN). The selector matches Mailcow's own
(`DKIM_SELECTOR = "dkim"`, `lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:44`). So password resets, invoices, dunning
warnings and suspension notices are no longer unsigned — this was for weeks the most expensive entry in
this document, and it is closed.

That clears the blocker under the verification gate, but the gate is **still off**:
`email_verification_enforced` defaults to `"false"` (`lib/settings.ts:106`) and
`emailVerificationError()` returns `null` before it probes anything else
(`lib/email-verification.ts:138`). Arming it makes *"our email arrived"* a precondition for taking
money, so it must not be flipped on an unproven inbox.

**The one step left before arming it:** send a real message through `lib/mailer.ts` to a large provider
and confirm the receiver reports `dkim=pass` — the record resolving is necessary, an actual delivery is
the proof. Then set `email_verification_enforced` to `true`; nothing else needs to change, the whole
feature is already built and wired. Details: **Business email hosting and DKIM**, and gaps 1 and 9 in
Known gaps.

**2. Every backup exists on exactly one chassis — off-site replication is unconfigured, and visibly so
by design.** `OFFSITE_RSYNC_TARGET` and `OFFSITE_RCLONE_REMOTE` in `/etc/nxeon/backup-offsite.env` are
both unset (the file is comments only), so `scripts/backup-offsite.sh` writes
`{"ok":false,"configured":false,…}` to `/tank/backup/status/offsite.json` and exits non-zero, leaving
`nxeon-backup-offsite.service` in a deliberate `failed` state (confirmed 2026-07-27: `failed`, status
`configured:false`, so the gap shows up in `systemctl` rather than silently). `/tank` is one pool in one
chassis; a chassis loss loses every customer backup **and** the platform's own DR set. Set exactly one
of the two variables — not both, which the script refuses — and the timer starts replicating. Gap 2 in
Known gaps.

**3. `nxeon_staging`'s database schema is behind its own tree, so the staging billing page 500s.**
`/opt/nxeon-staging` carries the current `schema.prisma` (card columns at `:147-148`,
`Invoice.stripePaymentIntentId` at `:466`) but `nxeon_staging` does not: `User` has 26 columns and
none of `cardBrand`, `cardLast4` or `defaultPaymentMethodId`, and `Invoice.stripePaymentIntentId`
does not exist. `/dashboard/billing` reads those columns, so it errors, and **the saved-card feature
cannot be exercised on staging at all** — which is the one feature staging most needs to rehearse.

A dump was taken first: `/root/db-backups/nxeon_staging-pre-schema-sync-20260726-223109.sql`
(301 KB, 2026-07-26 22:31). The fix is one command:

```bash
cd /opt/nxeon-staging && npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss
```

`--accept-data-loss` is required only because the push adds two unique constraints, and **both are
safe on this database**: `Mailbox.address @unique` — `select count(*) from "Mailbox"` in
`nxeon_staging` returns **0**, so there is nothing to collide; and `Invoice.stripePaymentIntentId
@unique` — a brand-new column, therefore all-NULL, and Postgres unique indexes do not constrain
NULLs. Run it against **`nxeon_staging` only**; never point a `prisma db push` at `nxeon`.

---

## What Nxeon is

Nxeon is a self-hosted, Hostinger-style VPS hosting business. A visitor lands on the marketing site,
picks a plan and a term, pays, and about ninety seconds later has root on a real KVM virtual
machine — plus, from the same portal, domains, TLS, mailboxes, block storage, backups, game servers,
a web console, an AI build assistant, and a one-click lift-and-shift migration from whatever host
they are leaving.

It all runs on **one** dedicated server:

- **Hypervisor**: Proxmox VE 9 on an OVH KS-GAME (i7-7700K, 64 GB RAM). Storage is a 2×450 GB NVMe
  ZFS mirror (pool `data`, 358 G) for live VM disks and a 4 TB HDD pool (`tank`, 3.6 T) for backups.
- **Guests**: customer VMs cloned from cloud-init templates VMID 9000–9009, plus VMID **8000
  `nxeon-mail`** — the Mailcow appliance carrying every mailbox on the platform: the transactional
  sender *and* paid customer business email.
- **Web, worker and Postgres run on the Proxmox host itself**, not in a VM.

The product surface, in one view:

```
 MARKETING  app/(marketing)        CUSTOMER PORTAL  app/dashboard      ADMIN  app/admin
 ──────────────────────────        ───────────────────────────────     ──────────────────
 /  pricing  vps  domains          servers   deploy    migrate         servers   users
 game-servers  business-email      volumes   ssl       domains         plans     products
 block-storage  migrate            mail      calendar  email           invoices  billing
 vibe-coding  compare  blog        games     build     claude-code     jobs  nodes  ips
 tools/*  (12 free tools)          billing   invoices  team            domains   mail
 legal/*  status  help             support   settings  refer           support   abuse
                                   projects  activity  feedback        docs      settings
```

Three properties to internalise before you touch anything:

- **Nothing mutates a VM from the web tier.** Every state change is a `Job` row the worker picks up.
  The web app may *read* Proxmox freely; it may not write. This is why "I clicked the button and
  nothing happened" is nearly always a worker question, not a web question.
- **One in-flight job per server, and the worker is strictly serial.** A 24-minute migration blocks
  every other customer's SSL issuance behind it. That is a real, unfixed design limit — see Known
  gaps.
- **Money is integer cents everywhere.** `balanceCents`, `priceCents`, `amountCents`. There are no
  floats in the billing path.

## Architecture at a glance

```
                                 INTERNET
                                     │
     :80 :443 ───────────────────────┼────────────── :25 :465 :587 :993 :4190
        │                            │                         │
   ┌────▼────────────────────────────────────────────┐          │

## Deploy wizard — ordering a VPS

**What it does.** A six-step form that turns a plan choice into a running VM. It is the only
customer path that creates a `Server` row.

```

**Workflow.**

```

   │  POST → payAndDeploy()            lib/actions.ts

   ├─ vpsTerm(termMonths)                            lib/billing-terms.ts
   ├─ regularPlanCents = vpsTermPriceCents(...)      lib/order.ts:135

   ▼

   │
   ├── cardCents === 0 ─────────────────► placeOrder() straight away

   ▼

   ├─ debitWallet(total)
   ├─ db.server.create({ ... autoBackup, extraDiskGB, expiresAt, termMonths })
   └─ db.job.create({ type: "PROVISION" })
   ▼

   ├─ nextVmid(), allocateIp(), allocateSshPort()   lib/ipam.ts

```

**Entry points.**

| Concern | Location |
|---|---|
| Wizard component (steps at `:167`) | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:109` |
| Enter-key submit block (a customer once deployed by pressing Enter) | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:409-413` |
| Form-level submit refusal — the real consent net | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:434-435` |
| Review step | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:785`, heading `:841` |
| Intent parsing from `FormData` | `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:130` |
| Quote (the price shown) | `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:186` |
| Order (the price charged) | `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:235` |
| The sold price, stamped once | `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:86` (`OrderPrice`), `:95`, parsed back at `:108` |
| `Server` row creation | `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:335` |
| Wallet/card split | `/opt/nxeon/lib/wallet-split.ts` |

**Data model.** `Server` (`prisma/schema.prisma:299`) with `planId`, `osTemplateId`, `termMonths`,
`expiresAt`, `extraDiskGB`, `addons` JSON, `autoBackup`, `backupIntervalHours`, `isFree`,
`wantsDedicatedIp`. Plus one `Job{type: PROVISION}`.

**Failure modes.**

| Mode | What the customer sees | Where it is handled |
|---|---|---|
| Insufficient wallet balance | "Insufficient balance." | `InsufficientBalanceError` → `OrderError`, `lib/order.ts:377` |
| Card cleared, `placeOrder` throws | Notification "Payment received — we couldn't finish setting up your server", money left in wallet | `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` order branch |
| Customer closes tab before redirect | Nothing visible; the **webhook** fulfils independently | `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` |
| No free IP / VMID in pool | `PROVISION` job FAILED, server `ERROR` | `lib/ipam.ts`, `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` |
| Clone succeeds, guest agent never answers | Server `RUNNING` but no SSH | Look at `journalctl -u nxeon-worker` for the clone task id |

**Diagnosis.** `/admin/jobs` → find the `PROVISION` row → read `Job.error` and `Job.step`. If the
job is `DONE` but the customer cannot connect, check `PortForward` for the server and compare with
`iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD -n`; `worker/network.ts` rebuilds that chain from the DB, so a
mismatch means the sync did not run.

**The consent net, and why it is at the form level.** For a while this wizard **charged four steps
early**: clicking *Continue →* on the Access step placed the order outright, at the default term,
before any total or Review screen. The customer-journey rehearsal reproduced it five times — five
servers, five wallet debits, no price ever shown (`docs/QA-JOURNEY.md:28-60`). The cause was React
reconciliation, not a missing check: *Continue* and *Deploy* were the two branches of an **unkeyed
ternary at the same position in the tree**, so React patched attributes onto one shared `<button>`
node — advancing the step removed Continue's `type="button"`, the live node became a submit control
mid-click, and the browser submitted. The pre-existing guard only ever covered the Enter key, while
asserting in its own comment that "Deploy only ever happens via the explicit button".

Fixed at the cause (distinct `key`s, explicit `type` on both branches) **and** given a net that does
not depend on getting JSX reconciliation right: the form refuses to submit anywhere but the Review
step (`DeployWizard.tsx:434-435`; incident recorded at `:424-433`). Pinned by
`test/purchase-consent.test.ts`. The lesson generalises — *a guard that describes the only way a
thing can happen is not a guard.*

**Why the Deploy button now says why it is disabled.** `canDeploy` (`:355`) folds four conditions
into one silent boolean, and the hostname field sits between two fields explicitly marked *optional*.
The rehearsal reached Review showing `Hostname —` and a greyed-out Deploy with nothing on the page
saying why — four steps back from the cause, on the last screen of the funnel. There are now three
named blockers — `accessBlocker` (`:372`), `deployBlocker` (`:383`), `primaryBlocker` (`:392`) —
rendered next to the disabled button, and *Continue* is gated on the Access step so the dead end is
never reached.

**Honest note.** The `addons` bridge is fixed but was broken for a long time. `lib/order.ts:337-346`
carries the whole story: the wizard sold "Daily backups", stored `addons.dailyBackup`, and nothing
read it, while the real scheduler keys off `autoBackup` + `backupIntervalHours`. Every server in the
live DB carried the add-on with `autoBackup: false`. It is now bridged at the point of sale
(`autoBackup: !!intent.addonBackup` at `:345`, `backupIntervalHours: 24`).

## Plans, terms and pricing

**What it does.** A `Plan` is a CPU/RAM/disk/bandwidth tier with one monthly price. A **term**
applies a commitment discount on top. A **promo** applies a seasonal discount on top of that.

Term ladder — `/opt/nxeon/lib/billing-terms.ts:9`:

| Term | `months` | Discount | $8.99/mo plan → effective |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly | 1 | 0% | $8.99/mo |
| Annual | 12 | 10% | $8.09/mo |
| Biennial | 24 | 15% | $7.64/mo |
| Triennial | 36 | 20% | $7.19/mo |

Domains have their own ladder (`DOMAIN_TERMS`, 1/2/3 years at 0/5/10%).

The three pricing functions, and this is the whole contract:

```
vpsTermPriceCents(monthly, months)   = round(monthly × months × (1 − disc))
                                       → what is CHARGED
vpsEffectiveMonthly(monthly, months) = round(termPrice / months)
                                       → what is DISPLAYED as "$/mo"
promoPriceCents(cents, promo)        = seasonal discount on top   lib/promotions.ts
```

Renewals bill `vpsTermPriceCents` **unchanged** — the promo applies to the first term only. That is
stated in the comment at `/opt/nxeon/lib/order.ts:199-201`, and the wizard's term cards now print
both numbers (`{total} first term · then {regTotal}`, `DeployWizard.tsx:816-825`) rather than the
first-term figure under a "billed every 1 yr" label. They used to print only the promo price, which
was wrong on 100% of orders, because `currentPromo()` never returns null.

**Entry points.** Term table and maths `/opt/nxeon/lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS` at `:9`,
`vpsTermPriceCents` at `:21`); promo `/opt/nxeon/lib/promotions.ts` (`currentPromo` `:115`,
`promoPriceCents` `:139`, `deepestPromoPercent` `:152`); **what a renewal costs**
`/opt/nxeon/lib/renewal-charge.ts:43` — see the Renewals chapter, it is the only definition; admin
plan CRUD `/opt/nxeon/app/admin/plans`; catalog seed `/opt/nxeon/prisma/catalog.ts`. Guarded by
`/opt/nxeon/test/billing-terms.test.ts` and `/opt/nxeon/test/pricing-display-vs-charge.test.ts`.

**Data model.** `Plan` (`prisma/schema.prisma:253`): `slug`, `cpuCores`, `ramMB`, `diskGB`,
`bandwidthTB`, `priceCents`, `storageTier` (`nvme` | `hdd`), `active`, `sortOrder`. `GamePlan`
(`:777`) layers a game tier on top of a base `Plan`. `Server.termMonths` records which term was
bought.

**Failure mode that actually happened.** The wizard displayed $8.99 and charged $6.29 because the
promo was applied on one side only. Both sides now apply it — but by *duplication*, not by sharing
one function: `promoPriceCents` is reimplemented client-side in the wizard
(`components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx:154`) rather than imported.

**The card leg is now bound; the wallet leg is not.** `createOrderCheckout` stamps the whole quote
into Stripe metadata as `nxeonOrderPrice` (`lib/stripe.ts:109`), the confirm route parses it back
(`:264`) and `placeOrder` takes it as `sold` (`lib/order.ts:238`, applied at `:245-247`), so a card
order settles at the price it was **sold** at rather than at a price recomputed after the card has
cleared. `payAndDeploy`'s wallet-only branch calls `placeOrder(user, intent)` with no `sold`
(`lib/actions.ts:475`) and re-quotes from its own `new Date()`, so a promo boundary crossed between
the Review screen and the click still moves the number. That is the residual half of gap 26 in
Known gaps.

**Diagnosis.** For "I was charged the wrong amount": read the `Invoice.lineItems` (they spell out
term and promo), then re-run the maths by hand with `vpsTermPriceCents` and the promo that was live
at `Invoice.createdAt`. `AuditLog` action `server.order` records `plan=`, `term=`, `extraDisk=`.

## Wallet, checkout and the wallet/card split

**What it does.** Every customer has a single integer-cent balance, `User.balanceCents`. All
purchases debit the wallet; a card is used only to make up a shortfall. That inversion — wallet
first, card for the remainder — is the platform's core payment shape and it recurs in checkout,
resize, disk expansion and renewals.

## Server migration — what it is and how a run unfolds

**The flagship.** A customer enters their old server's IP and root password, picks a target Nxeon
VPS, and the platform lifts their entire stack across: files at the same absolute paths, databases
with users and grants, Docker images and containers, systemd units, crontabs, web-server
configuration regenerated for the target, TLS issued, and then a verification gate that HTTP-probes
every hostname the old server actually served before it will call the run a success.

It is 5,351 lines in `/opt/nxeon/worker/migrate-real.ts` and it earned every one of them. The failure
catalogue in `docs/MIGRATION-FIELD-NOTES.md` has 28 numbered entries, all observed against real
customer servers.

**Two different things share the word "migration."** Do not confuse them:

| | Customer lift-and-shift | Platform self-move |
|---|---|---|
| Code | `worker/migrate-real.ts`, `worker/migrate-detect.ts`, `worker/migrate.ts`, `lib/actions-migrate.ts` | `docs/MIGRATION.md`, `scripts/migrate-export.sh`, `scripts/migrate-repoint-dns.sh` |

## Backups — daily, keep 3, and platform vs customer archives

**Two completely separate backup systems share one 4 TB pool, and keeping them separate is a
data-loss-prevention control, not tidiness.**

```
 /tank  (3.6 T, HDD pool)
 │
 ├── /tank/backup/dump ─────────── PVE storage "backup"  ← CUSTOMER on-demand
 │        vzdump-qemu-102-*.zst      + scheduled backups
 │        addressable via the Proxmox storage-content API
 │        retention: CUSTOMER_BACKUP_KEEP = 2   worker/index.ts:39
 │        pruned by pruneBackups(conn, vmid, 2) after each success  :761
 │
 ├── /tank/backup/platform ─────── NOT the dump/ subdir of ANY PVE storage
 │        vzdump-qemu-<vmid>-*.zst  ← PLATFORM disaster recovery
 │        host-config-*.tar.gz      ← /etc/pve + VM definitions
 │        written by scripts/backup-vms.sh  --dumpdir
 │        retention: NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP = 3, via vzdump --prune-backups
 │        ► Proxmox only indexes <storage>/dump, so these have NO volid.
 │          They are not "filtered out" of the customer prune — they are
 │          NOT ADDRESSABLE by it.
 │
 ├── /tank/backup/db ───────────── nightly pg_dump, nxeon + nxeon_staging
 ├── /tank/backup/status ───────── JSON health files (see the honest note)
 └── /tank/backup/snippets ─────── cloud-init vendor data
```

**Why this matters.** The incident is documented at `/opt/nxeon/lib/proxmox.ts:403-437` and in the
header of `/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-vms.sh:12-33`. Platform archives used to land in the same PVE
storage as customer backups, and `pruneBackups` selected deletion victims on nothing but
`b.vmid === vmid`. On 2026-07-26, vmid 102 ended the 04:31 platform run holding two archives — the
customer's own manual one and the platform's 10 GB DR copy — and **the customer's very next click on
"Create backup" would have deleted the platform's copy of their VM.** Repeated across the fleet, that
silently destroys the entire bare-metal recovery set, one customer click at a time.

The fix is three independent layers, in order of strength (`lib/proxmox.ts:415-437`):

1. **Structural** — platform archives live outside every PVE storage, so no `volid` exists that a
   customer-triggered `DELETE /storage/backup/content/<volid>` could resolve to them.
2. **Chokepoint** — `deleteBackup` is the only function in the repo that issues a storage-content
   DELETE. It re-derives protection for every volid immediately before deleting, refuses on the PVE
   `protected` attribute, the platform notes marker, or the protection registry, and **fails closed**
   if it cannot determine the answer.
3. **Marker + registry** — if the platform job is ever re-pointed at a shared PVE storage it stamps
   each archive with `--notes-template` carrying `PLATFORM_BACKUP_MARKER` and appends the volid to a
   protection registry. Both are honoured, which also covers archives already written before layer 1
   existed.

**Schedule.**

| Job | Unit | When | Retention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Whole-system (host config + every guest) | `nxeon-backup-vms.timer` | daily ~04:30 | keep 3 (`NXEON_VM_BACKUP_KEEP`) |
| PostgreSQL logical dumps | `nxeon-backup-db.timer` | daily ~03:15 | 14 days |
| Restore verification | `nxeon-verify-restore.timer` | daily ~05:30 | — |
| Off-site replication | `nxeon-backup-offsite.timer` | daily ~04:20 | — |
| Customer scheduled backups | worker sweep, 15 min | per `backupIntervalHours` | keep 2 |
